_sources.discrepancies: NCSL lists TN as 'strict photo ID'. SoS confirms voters without acceptable photo ID must vote a provisional ballot; provisional ballot is not counted unless voter presents acceptable ID by the close of business on the second business day after the election. Consistent. 2026-06-10 verification: August 6, 2026 primary and November 3, 2026 general CONFIRMED (TN SoS election schedule; FVAP 2026 primary calendar current as of May 2026 concurs). Early-voting windows match the statutory 20-days-to-5-days rule (primary July 17-Aug 1; general Oct 14-29); registration deadlines match the 30-day rule (July 7 / Oct 5). Corrected accepted-ID list: per sos.tn.gov/elections/photo-id, college student IDs are NOT acceptable in Tennessee (the file previously listed them as acceptable), and TN/federal photo IDs are acceptable even if expired (the file previously said IDs must not be expired).

earlyVoting.notes: Early voting begins 20 days before the primary (July 17, 2026) and ends 5 days before (August 1, 2026). Hours and sites are set by each county election commission.
Early voting begins 20 days before Election Day (October 14, 2026) and ends 5 days before (October 29, 2026). Hours and sites are set by each county election commission.
Early voting runs from 20 days to 5 days before Election Day. Hours and locations vary by county.

acceptedIds: Tennessee driver's license or photo ID card
Photo ID issued by Tennessee or federal government
Tennessee handgun carry permit with photo
votingRules.idNote: College student IDs and photo IDs not issued by the federal or Tennessee state government (such as county or city IDs and library cards) are NOT acceptable: https://sos.tn.gov/elections/photo-id
votingRules.expirationRule: A Tennessee or federal photo ID may be used even if expired, except student IDs are not acceptable. Confirm details with the TN Secretary of State: https://sos.tn.gov/elections/photo-id
votingRules.impedimentDeclaration: Strict photo ID state: voters without acceptable photo ID must cast a provisional ballot and present acceptable ID to the county election commission by close of business on the second business day after the election for it to be counted.
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Tennessee prohibits the use of mobile phones in the voting booth. You may not photograph your marked ballot.
additionalRules: Open primary: any registered voter may choose which party's primary to vote in; party registration is not required.
No legislative primary runoffs in Tennessee.

eligibility: Will be outside the county on Election Day and during the early voting period
Have a specific illness or physical disability
Hospitalized as an emergency patient within 5 days before the election
A caretaker of a person confined due to illness or disability
A resident of a licensed care facility
Enrolled in college outside the county
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: Must be received by the county election commission 7 days before the election
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the county election commission by the close of polls on Election Day
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Absentee ballot must arrive at the county election commission by the close of polls on Election Day.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Tennessee has an open primary in practice (Tenn. Code Ann. §2-7-115). There is no party registration in Tennessee. Voters may request either party's primary ballot at the polls without any restriction.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Tennessee tiene una primaria abierta en la práctica (Tenn. Code Ann. §2-7-115). Tennessee no tiene registro de partido. Los votantes pueden solicitar la boleta de primaria de cualquier partido en el lugar de votación sin ninguna restricción.
